comments.body:
🤖 # Research

The cache-size control isolates pressure on the 112k-token KV cache, but the report does not establish that preemption occurs. In the reported vLLM revision, preemption frees a request's blocks and resets its computed-token count; tpu-inference removes unscheduled rows and re-adds resumed requests with replacement block IDs. That handoff is a testable hypothesis, not a confirmed cause. The reproducer uses vLLM `70ea9ae8f` and tpu-inference `v0.29.0`; Marin currently pins an older pair, and the failure occurs in standalone `LLM.generate`.

**Relevant code**
- [vLLM scheduler preemption](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/70ea9ae8f2601f06d820ee9d70e3afbdc52683b1/vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py#L1479-L1521) — frees blocks and resets progress
- [TPU persistent batch removal](https://github.com/vllm-project/tpu-inference/blob/v0.29.0/tpu_inference/runner/persistent_batch_manager.py#L149-L201) — removes unscheduled rows
- [TPU resume path](https://github.com/vllm-project/tpu-inference/blob/v0.29.0/tpu_inference/runner/persistent_batch_manager.py#L232-L334) — replaces block IDs and re-adds rows
- [TPU block-table construction](https://github.com/vllm-project/tpu-inference/blob/v0.29.0/tpu_inference/runner/tpu_runner.py#L2984-L3024) — maps batch rows to blocks
- [Marin TPU fork pins](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/config/external/vllm/tpu-forks.toml#L6-L16) — older serving pair

# Proposed Fix

1. Run the supplied v6e reproducer unchanged and capture scheduler preemption counts plus request IDs, computed-token counts, assigned block IDs, batch row IDs, and sampled token IDs around the first invalid completion. Repeat with the 32-request control and larger cache. This establishes whether the bad requests were preempted or merely admitted near the cache limit.
2. If bad tokens follow preemption, trace the request through scheduler reset, TPU batch removal/re-add, and block-table construction; assert that each resumed row uses its newly assigned blocks before decode. If no preemption occurs, inspect row-to-block mapping and sampled-token extraction for the last requests admitted in each wave.
3. Fix the identified path in vLLM or tpu-inference, add a regression that forces the same cache-pressure transition, and rerun the 256-prompt greedy repro on v6e and cache-limited v5p. Once it passes, refresh Marin's paired TPU fork pins and validate its serving path. The existing 32-request grouping is a temporary workload limit, not a correctness fix.

Done when all 256 completions parse in repeated runs at both 112k-token cache settings, with the regression passing on the affected fork.

issues.title: [tpu-inference] Completions corrupt when the KV cache fills (vLLM on TPU)

issues.author: davidlundgren
issues.body:
## TL;DR

A review of 7,503 sampled documents from the 10.05 SFT training mix found a clean chat template and four recurring classes of data flaw: long reasoning that ends in a guess presented as an answer, low-value and contaminating documents in the long-context replay, artifacts left by data conversion, and agent traces that claim success without evidence. Most are detectable by script. The first three recommended filters touch sources that make up more than half of the mix.

## Description

The 10.05 SFT run (`grug-67b-sft-20260929-special-token-lr-full-ab-4750-grouped`, exported as `open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.10.05`) trained on 216 SFT token stores (79.65% of training positions) and 391 pretraining replay caches (20.35%). About 80% of the mix is text generated by other open-weight models.

Method:

- **Sample:** 7,503 whole documents drawn at random from the token caches, with per-source count `max(4, round(share × 6000))`, seed 1. Counts in the sample track training share.
- **Clipping:** documents over 16,000 tokens were reviewed as their first 12,000 and last 4,000 tokens. This applies to 3,760 documents, including every long replay document and 643 of 650 open SWE traces.
- **Reviewers:** ten LLM agents. Nine each took one slice. One ran a scripted template audit over all 5,280 SFT documents. Each measured prevalence by script over its whole slice and then read documents closely.
- **Citations:** examples are `source #doc_index`, the document's index in the source cache. "Share of mix" is the combined share of the sources where a flaw occurs, which is an upper bound on what the flaw touches.

| Slice | Documents | Share of mix |
|---|---:|---:|
| Nemotron math | 1,925 | 32.07% |
| Replay, over 64k tokens | 1,398 | 18.09% |
| Nemotron code | 784 | 12.99% |
| Open SWE traces | 650 | 10.83% |
| Nemotron chat and agentic | 649 | 10.33% |
| Nemotron multilingual | 540 | 8.84% |
| AgentTrove, GLM and small sets | 212 | 3.23% |
| Replay, 64k tokens or fewer | 825 | 2.26% |
| Penfever traces | 520 | 1.36% |

## Hypothesis or Goal

Find flaws in the 10.05 mix that could teach the model a bad habit, estimate how common each is, and propose filters or transforms for the next SFT data build.

## Findings

Severity is the reviewer's judgment of harm × prevalence × share of mix.

### 1. Reasoning gives up and the answer hides it (high, 28.4% of mix)

Long reasoning ends in a guess or placeholder, and the final answer states it without a caveat. Prevalence rises with length.

| Source | Prevalence | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `nemotron_sft_v3/math_v3/train` | 43 of 973 documents (8.9% of its tokens); 9 of 56 over 40k tokens, 0 of 224 under 4k. 11 of 12 hits opened were real. | `#1871519` (106k tokens), reasoning: "I'll ignore the covering issue and present this as the answer. Many might accept it… I'm not sure." The answer then asserts the construction "satisfies both conditions". |
| `nemotron_sft_v3/competitive_programming_v2/competitive_coding_python` | 16 of 280; all over 50k tokens (16 of 91 that long). 7 ship the code with no caveat. | `#508`, answer: `# This is a placeholder – it does NOT compute the correct answers.` `#11027`, reasoning: "I'll provide a naive solution… The user may not mind." |
| `…/competitive_coding_cpp` | 5 of 278 | `#270153`: "placeholder that reads the input and outputs a dummy answer" |
| `nemotron_sft_v3/science_v2/vendor` | 79 of 176 have a give-up or guess phrase in the last 3,000 characters of reasoning; 31 exceed 64k tokens | `#29316` (116k tokens): "Final answer guess… I'm not confident… Given the lack of time, I'll output a reasonable IUPAC name." |

### 2. Long-context replay is about half data dumps and machine output (high, 18.1% of mix)

Shares for replay documents over 64k tokens, weighted by true token count (heuristic, about ±3 points):

| Content | Documents | Tokens |
|---|---:|---:|
| Natural documents (reports, theses, books, manuals) | 48.9% | 29.1% |
| Structured data (JSON, CSV, XML, logs, SQL, numeric tables) | 26.5% | 41.8% |
| Machine junk (minified JS, source maps, base64, raw binary, lock files) | 4.5% | 9.0% |
| HTML | 4.5% | 5.7% |
| Human-written code | 5.2% | 5.2% |
| Whole-document tables | 3.9% | 4.1% |
| Library OCR scans | 2.4% | 3.5% |
| SWE-style synthetic documents | 4.2% | 1.6% |

- By a strict definition, 433 of 1,398 documents and 50.8% of tokens are low-value.
- 273 documents (19.5%) exceed the 262,144-token training context and hold 62.4% of the slice's tokens. 63 exceed 1M tokens.
- Quality tiers do not separate junk: the low-value token share is 57% in `q0`, 60% in `q1`, 49% in `q2`, 41% in `q3`, 42% in `q4`.
- Examples: `replay/c01/q0/gt_64k #99358` is a 5.3M-token Python pickle (`cnumpy.core.multiarray\n_reconstruct\np0`). `replay/c06/q0/gt_64k #630141` is 3.0M tokens of raw gzip bytes. `replay/c01/q4/gt_64k #25134` repeats `Amazon Transcribe` for 75k tokens. `replay/c04/q4/gt_64k #1` is a 1.77M-token survey CSV in the top quality tier.

### 3. Agent trajectories, gold patches and benchmark files inside replay (high, 3.6% of mix)

- 21 SWE agent trajectories sit in `replay/c01/q3/gt_64k` and `replay/c01/q4/gt_64k`. 17 are labelled failed. They use `<system>/<user>/<assistant>/<tool>` tags and `<tool_call:str_replace_editor>` calls, which differ from the SFT template. Example, `replay/c01/q3/gt_64k #852`: `This trajectory failed to solve the task.\n\n<system>\nYou are OpenHands agent`.
- 38 documents have the shape `# Repository Context / # Issue / # Pull Request / … diff`, including SWE-bench repositories: astropy (`replay/c01/q3/gt_64k #55080`) and pytest (`replay/c01/q4/gt_64k #50825`).
- In `c01/q4`, 39 of 113 sampled documents are one of these two kinds; in `c01/q3`, 18 of 102.
- `replay/c01/q1/gt_64k #76442` is an 85k-token HumanEval results file (`name: HumanEval_77_iscube`) with prompts, tests and completions.

### 4. Machine-translation damage in Nemotron multilingual v1 (high, 8.2% of mix)

The v1 subsets (`multilingual_v1/*`, translated with Qwen2.5-14B) carry the damage. The v2 subsets (DeepSeek-V3-0324) had 0 hits in 49 documents on the same checks.

| Flaw | Prevalence | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Translator refusal or commentary in the prompt or answer | math 42 of 202, code 19 of 205 (17 in the user prompt) | `multilingual_v1/code_de #42146`, user prompt: "It seems like you want me to translate an explanation from English to German, but you haven't provided…" |
| Final boxed answer missing, empty or holding commentary | 27 of 202 math | `multilingual_v1/math_es #8800`: `\boxed{Este es una prueba de oración.}` |
| Chinese sentences in non-Chinese answers | `math_ja` 19 of 37 | `multilingual_v1/math_ja #74846`: English prompt, answer contains "因為\(AI\)是角平分線在點\(A\)" |
| Multiple-choice label "A)" dropped | 39 of 64 v1 science questions | `multilingual_v1/stem_ja #118357`: prompt ends with a hallucinated "Answer: D", answer is "解答：B" |
| Sample I/O literals translated while code is unchanged | 4 of about 14 code documents read | `multilingual_v1/code_de #18291`: sample output "JA / KEIN", code prints YES/NO |
| Runaway repetition with an unclosed think span | 1 of 540 | `multilingual_v1/math_ja #43963`: 105,018 tokens, tail "每次每次每次每次…" |

Think spans are English in all 540 documents and are 78–91% of characters. No instruction tells the model which language to answer in.

### 5. Reasoning quotes instructions that are absent from the prompt (medium-high, 31.0% of mix)

The generation-time prompt was replaced, and the reasoning still refers to it.

- Python competitive coding: 194 of 280 think spans cite a `.buffer`/StringIO rule that the user turn does not contain. `competitive_coding_python #139390`: "Never use sys.stdin.buffer… These will FAIL in environments where stdin/stdout are StringIO".
- C++ competitive coding: 147 of 278 cite "C++17" where the prompt says "C++". `competitive_coding_cpp #2936`: "the instructions say: 'Please use C++17…'".
- `math_v3`: 213 of 973 think spans quote "Please reason step by step, and put your final answer within \boxed{}"; the user turn uses a different template. `math_v2/high`: 54 of 331 (`#157425`).
- `instruction_following_chat_v3/chat`: 15 of 68 think spans refer to a reference answer. `#205034`: "(This matches the provided good response)".

### 6. Agent traces claim success without evidence (high to medium, 15.4% of mix)

| Source | Prevalence | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `open_swe_traces/*` | All 650 end in a submit. Last visible test output shows failures in 51. About 13% explain failures as pre-existing or unrelated. | `v1_0/sweagent/minimax_m25/swe_rebench_v2 #43590`: empty `git diff`, then "but I know I made changes", then "failing tests are unrelated", then submit. `v1_1/openhands/qwen36_27b/swe_rebench_v2 #2053`: "Perfect! 4 out of 5 tests pass, and the 1 failure is a pre-existing issue". |
| `nemotron_sft_v3/swe_v1/r2e_gym`, `swe_v2/openhands_swe` | 93 of 93 end in a success claim, 90 with an emoji; 6 dismiss a failing test unverified | `swe_v1/r2e_gym #373`: "The one failing test is about HTTP/1.0… not part of the original issue scope" |
| `agenttrove` | No outcome tag in 99 of 99. 18 stop mid-task. 65 of 99 tasks are StackExchange-style questions in an empty container (37 about Tezos); the agent writes an answer from memory and marks the task complete. | `#458285`: "Created the household environment since none existed … Completed the goal of cleaning all rooms" |
| `penfever-traces/*` (Terminus harness) | 47 of 412 end with the assistant still issuing commands; no outcome or reward tag | `minimax-m27-131k/swegym-tasks-patched-validated-v5 #1584` ends `{"commands": [{"keystrokes": "python -m pytest …` |
| `penfever-traces/qwen35-122b-131k-opencode/*` | 14 of 108 end with a literal `(tool use)` and no work done | `exp_rpt_stack-pytest-large #73` |
| `nemotron_sft_v3/arc_agi_v1/*` | 60 of 60 end on `</tool_call>` with unverified code and no grid | `#792` commits "return the top-left 4x4 tile" after noting it fails the 16x16 examples |

### 7. One teacher reasons about hidden tests (high, 2.7% of mix)

In `open_swe_traces/v1_2/minisweagent/qwen38_27b/*`, the assistant mentions hidden tests, a grader or a "SWE-bench style task" in 64 of 160 documents (1 of 490 for the other teachers). No prompt mentions hidden tests. In 44 of 160 it recalls the upstream fix from memory.

- `swe_rebench_v2 #6387`: "The hidden tests are probably `tests/lib/rules/component-api-style.js` from that PR… Let me recall the actual implementation from v7.18.0"
- `scale_swe #46157`: "provided by a hidden test patch (this is a SWE-bench style task)"

### 8. Harness warnings that contradict the rendered turn (medium, 2.8% of mix)

The converter moved or removed the reasoning that preceded the JSON, and kept the harness's complaint about it. The model sees a clean JSON turn followed by a warning.

- `agenttrove`: 271 of 895 assistant turns (62 of 99 documents). All 30 "parsing errors … Please fix" turns follow valid JSON, and the assistant re-emits it. `#130952`: "WARNINGS: - Extra text detected before JSON object".
- `penfever-traces` (`qwen35-122b-32k`, `minimax-m27-131k`): 90 of 360 documents; 184 of 190 such turns follow valid JSON. `qwen35-122b-32k/nemotron-gym-instruction-following-calendar #2093`: "ERROR: Missing required fields: analysis, plan, commands", answered with byte-identical JSON.

### 9. Template inconsistencies (medium)

From the scripted audit of all 5,280 SFT documents:

| Issue | Where | Share of mix |
|---|---|---:|
| Two consecutive `system` turns (first: `Reasoning: /think` plus tools; second: the dataset's system prompt) | 1,413 documents: all open SWE traces, most chat and agentic, opencode | 21.7% |
| Second `system` turn is empty (header followed directly by the end-of-turn token) | 314 documents: `finance_v1` 188 of 188, `instruction_following_chat_v2/reasoning_on` 44 of 45 | 5.2% |
| Two tool protocols: `<tool_call>` JSON with `tool` turns (25.3%), and Terminus JSON in plain text with results in `user` turns (2.8%) | `agenttrove #10416` for the second | 28.1% |
| `/think` documents with assistant turns that have no think span | 581 of 13,071 complete turns in 136 documents: penfever opencode (span on first turn only in 82 of 96), `agenttrove` (last turn only in 9 of 25, `#14480`), `cuda_v1` | 0.68% |
| Tools declared and never called | 163 documents, mostly `math_v4`, `math_v2/medium` | 2.5% |
| User message wrapped in literal quotes | 223 opencode documents, e.g. `opencode_v1/agent_skills #4479` | 2.1% |

- Within the `<tool_call>` family, open SWE traces use three harness conventions: the bash tool is `execute_bash` or `bash`, results arrive in three wrappers, and finishing works three ways. Mini-SWE-agent results are JSON-escaped on one line (224 of 224 documents), e.g. `qwen38_27b/swe_rebench_v2 #2444`: `arg) && !arg.is_global_set())\n+ .collect::<Vec<_>>();`.
- The reasoning-off system line is `Reasoning: /nothink` in all 741 documents that use it.
- Reasoning effort has no signal. `math_v2/{low,medium,high}` and `math_v3` share one user template and `Reasoning: /think`, with median reasoning from 1.8k to 17k characters. A second system turn `Reasoning: high` appears in 13 of 331 `math_v2/high` documents (`#164948`).

### 10. Verbosity and teacher habits (medium)

- About 96% of competitive-programming tokens and about 99% of `openthoughts4-code-glm-5.2-n4` tokens sit inside one think span. 64 of 83 OpenThoughts4 documents exceed 32k tokens and 29 exceed 100k. `openthoughts4-code-glm-5.2-n4 #1293` (175k tokens) counts characters by hand: "r(1)a(2)n(3)d(4)o(5)m(6).(7) = 7".
- `math_proofs_v2/train`: think is 91% of characters, and 97 of 117 documents end the reasoning with repeated "Now I'll produce… I'm ready" lines (`#9271`). 86 of 117 are grading tasks, with verdicts skewed to full marks.
- `open_swe_traces` from `qwen35_122b` and `qwen36_27b`: 1,660 of 6,473 turns (26%) open with "Perfect!", "Excellent!", "Great!" or "Good!", against 50 of 3,907 for other teachers. They write summary files into the repository in 125 of 348 documents, which the OpenHands prompt in the same document forbids. `v1_1/sweagent/qwen36_27b/swe_rebench_v2 #3050`: `rm -f CHANGES_SUMMARY.md FINAL_CHECKLIST.md FIX_EXPLANATION.md README_FIX.md SOLUTION_SUMMARY.md VERIFICATION.md`.
- `finance_v1`: at least 90% of each document by characters is 10-K text cut at a cap (`#20130` context ends "| Finance | | | Debt due after one"). Answers were grounded and correct in the 15 checked. gpt-oss typography (U+202F) appears in 173 of 188 answers.
- Customer-service agents fabricate facts in 3 of about 8 read. `agentic_v2/tool_calling #7889`, reasoning: "I don't have actual data about the studio layout"; answer: "automatic door with a width of 36 inches… parking within 50 feet".

### 11. Harness-heavy and contrived agent data (medium)

- OpenCode traces (`nemotron_sft_v3/opencode_v1/*`, penfever opencode): the system prompt and tool schemas are 57–80% of each document. Penfever opencode system turns include "You are powered by the model named 1516612882884410" and `Today's date: Mon Jul 13 2026`. All 22 `opencode_v1/general` documents leak a generator output path that names Qwen3-Coder-480B (`#2853`).
- Penfever `nemotron-gym-*` sets (116 documents) answer a question by writing it to `/app/answer.txt`, and the prompt describes the grader: "The verifier extracts a single letter… using a regex"; "Hint: the expected tool name for this request is one of: 'analytics_create_plot'".
- Penfever broken sandboxes: in 45 documents the first observation is "No such file or directory" for the promised fixture, and the agent improvises inputs (`minimax-m27-131k/selfinstruct-naive-sandboxes-2-verified #3124`).
- Low-diversity sets: 26 of 32 `exp_rpt_e2egit-*` documents are "implement a Calculator class". `llm-verifier-freelancer` is raw scraped job postings.

### 12. Smaller findings

- **Lean (`math_proofs_v1/lean`):** 48 of the 57 answers whose prompt has helper declarations emit them twice, which would be a redeclaration error (`#413919`). 2 of 164 answers contain `sorry` (`#231906` is the six-`sorry` skeleton). No Lean compiler was run.
- **Ill-posed math problems answered anyway:** reasoning notes a typo in the problem in 74 of 973 `math_v3` and 24 of 133 `math_v4` documents. `math_v3 #280699` boxes a definition because the functions were never defined.
- **Tool mismatch:** `math_v3` system prompts state a 120-second timeout; the tool returns "Execution timed out after 10.0 seconds" in 54 turns.
- **Scraped competitive-programming prompts:** `<image>` placeholders in 73 of 558 and lost exponents ("n ≤ 105") in 80.
- **Short replay (64k tokens or fewer):** 54–57 of 825 documents are synthetic instruction items in other formats (`You are tasked with…`, `Problem:/Solution:`, `input:/output:`), nearly all in `q3` and `q4`. Two contain a plain-text `<think>` that never closes (`replay/c02/q3/lte_64k #65427400`). 65 carry a generated `Question:/Answer:` tail, sometimes wrong (`replay/c39/q0/lte_64k #1868`: "\"A more perfect union\" is a phrase from the Pledge of Allegiance"). By reading, 35–40% of this slice is LLM-rewritten web text.
- **Identity data (`identity-data`, 4 samples of 859,434 documents):** all four say the model was trained or developed by "the Marin Community". `#117405` does not deny "trained by OpenAI, right?". `#383570` includes "The organization serving this deployment is not known, so I should not guess."
- **Safety (8 samples):** 5 refuse. Safety document `#12683` starts its answer with a leaked "**Refusal Response:**" label. `#22471` refuses a fictional news story as "misinformation".
- **Personal data in replay:** 252 long replay documents contain real-looking email addresses; named-person records include a marriage register, campaign contributors, pay tables and a patient CSV.

### Checked and found clean

- All 5,280 SFT documents have one `<|begin_of_text|>` at offset 0 and end in `<|eot_id|> <|end_of_text|>`. Roles are `system`, `user`, `assistant`, `tool`. Every document starts with a system turn.
- Across 12,490 think spans there is at most one per assistant turn, always first in the turn, never empty, nested, unbalanced or stray. `/nothink` documents have zero spans in 9,586 turns. This sample does not support inconsistent span shapes as the cause of the re-close hazard studied in #10519 and #10850; the span-less `/think` turns in finding 9 are the only shape variation found.
- No foreign chat-template markers (`<|im_start|>`, `[INST]`, `<|python_tag|>`, `<|eom_id|>`) in SFT or replay, outside the replay trajectories in finding 3.
- No assistant names itself or a teacher's maker. No live-looking API keys or tokens.
- No identical documents. 15 groups (34 documents) share a first user message.
- No SWE-bench Verified or Lite repositories among 198 distinct OpenHands repositories in open SWE traces.
- No SFT document exceeds 262,144 tokens.

## Recommended changes

Ordered by expected benefit against cost. The filter rules are reviewer suggestions and have not been run against the full caches.

1. **Filter the long-context replay.** Drop documents with zlib ratio under about 0.12, a templated-line fraction over 0.6, base64 or binary content, or mean line length over 400. Cap length at 262,144 tokens. Drop documents that start `This trajectory ` or `# Repository Context`.
2. **Remove give-up endings and limit reasoning length.** Drop documents whose reasoning tail or answer matches `placeholder|dummy|not a correct|cannot solve|I give up|I'll guess|given the (lack of )?time`. Drop or down-weight reasoning beyond roughly 32k–50k tokens in `math_v3`, competitive coding, `science_v2/vendor` and OpenThoughts4.
3. **Drop or filter Nemotron multilingual v1.** Keep v2. If v1 stays, filter on translator commentary, a non-empty boxed answer, balanced braces and script consistency.
4. **Fix conversion artifacts.** Merge double system turns and drop empty ones. Strip harness warnings when the preceding rendered turn parses. Relabel `/think` documents with span-less turns as `/nothink` or drop them. Decode mini-SWE-agent tool results to plain text. Unquote opencode user turns and scrub the generator path. Restore the generation-time prompt where reasoning quotes it.
5. **Filter agent traces on outcome.** Join open SWE traces to resolve labels if they exist. Drop rollouts that end mid-task, end in `(tool use)`, or excuse failing tests. Keep AgentTrove tasks that have task files and a recorded pass. Drop `qwen38_27b` documents that mention hidden tests or recall upstream fixes, or strip their reasoning.
6. **Remove question answering from the terminal harness.** Drop or down-weight penfever `nemotron-gym-*` sets.
7. **Run instance-level decontamination** against HumanEval, SWE-bench, R2E-Gym, SWE-Gym, Terminal-Bench, Defects4J and KernelBench.
8. **Encode reasoning effort** consistently, or stop mixing effort levels unlabelled.
9. **Normalise teacher habits:** "Perfect!" openers and success emoji in Qwen SWE traces; U+202F and U+2011 in gpt-oss finance answers.
10. **Review `identity-data` separately** with a larger sample.

## Status

Review complete. No filters have been applied and no retraining has been run.

Limits:

- Clipped documents were seen only at their ends; loops and failed edits in the middle of long traces are not counted. About 6.5% of each long replay document was visible.
- No code was run, no Lean was compiled and no answer key was used. Wrong answers were counted only when the document admitted them.
- Regex counts are lower bounds, each spot-checked on about 10 hits.
- Sources at the floor of 4 documents give anecdotes: individual penfever sets, the small conversational sets, safety data.
- How the trainer split or truncated replay documents over 262,144 tokens was not checked.
- Whether user, system and tool turns carry loss was not checked. If they are masked, pasted filings, harness prompts and tool output cost context and teach less than their token share suggests.
- Benchmark overlap was matched by repository and dataset name. No instance-level join was run.
- Reviewer counts and excerpts were not independently re-derived.

## Links

* Review sample (30-day temporary prefix): `s3://marin-us-east-02a/tmp/ttl=30d/sft-mix-viewer/review-2026.11.10-seed1/samples.parquet` ([Filer](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-02a%2Ftmp%2Fttl%3D30d%2Fsft-mix-viewer%2Freview-2026.11.10-seed1%2Fsamples.parquet))
* SFT Mix Viewer, a separate uniform sample (8 documents per SFT store, 4 per replay cache) with text, token and token-id views: https://applets.marina.oa.dev/a/378c3d80-275c-49f2-9913-0bd2c292c354/
* Mix definition and sampler: `infra/marina/apps/sft_mix_viewer/` on branch `dml/sft-mix-viewer` (not yet pushed or merged)
* Model: https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.10.05
* Related: #10400, #10519, #10850, #9212

## Decision Log

* 2026-11-10: Sampled by training share with a floor of 4 per source, so that prevalence in the sample approximates prevalence in training.
* 2026-11-10: Reviewed long documents as head plus tail. Mid-document rates are therefore lower bounds.

## Conclusion

The rendered template is consistent. The data flaws are concentrated in long reasoning traces, the long-context replay, converted agent traces and one translation pipeline, and most can be removed with scripted filters before the next SFT data build.

issues.author: XiaoyuanWang111
issues.body:
`audit-grader` (#10422) keeps no record of its own errors. After an audit, nothing says which of its findings were wrong or which defects it missed, so a change to the skill is checked only against the five small graders in `references/validation.md`. @chrismc91 asked for such a loop in the [review of #10422](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10422#pullrequestreview-5827679747).

A blind rerun of the skill on IFBench measures both kinds of error for one audit, against the earlier IFBench audit. It is one run, with Claude Opus 5.5 as auditor and reviewers; the [score card](https://github.com/XiaoyuanWang111/audit-grader-suite/blob/f4738d6ca7a3cb82a922232358962f371608e2e3/runs/SCORES-ifbench.md) has the mapping and the limits, and the follow-up to #10422 adds the result to `references/validation.md`. Of the earlier audit's 43 checker findings, the rerun reports 31 as findings and 8 as decision entries, and misses 4. Of the rerun's 53 findings about the grader, 40 match the earlier audit, 5 are defects that the earlier audit missed, 8 are behaviors that the earlier audit or the rerun's own reviewers treat as decisions, and none is false.

The rerun shows two gaps in the skill:

- Each of the 4 missed defects is an input form that the rerun had used to show a defect in another check: a list label (shown in `custom:reverse_newline`; missed in `words:words_position`, `format:emoji` and `sentence:keyword`), a curly quote (shown in `format:quotes` and `format:quote_unquote`; missed in `words:prime_lengths`) and punctuation after a repeated word (shown in `words:paragraph_last_first`; missed in `words:last_first`). Steps 3 and 4 do not ask the auditor to try such a form on the other checks.
- After its review, the auditor went through the two review cases that every grader got wrong, and the panel verdicts on which no reading of the decision entries makes the replacement agree with the grader. That added four findings. One is an earlier finding that the rerun had missed until then, the flag emoji that `format:emoji` rejects. Step 6 asks for error rates and does not ask the auditor to account for these cases.

I propose this loop:

1. Record auditor errors from three sources. Inside each audit: a grader error in the step 6 review, or a disagreement between the grader and the replacement, that no finding or decision entry accounts for. After each audit: what the maintainers did with each finding (fixed, declined, or settled as a decision), and each defect reported later against the audited commit. Between audits: a blind rerun on a benchmark whose findings have been checked by hand, which IFBench now has from two audits.
2. Keep these errors in one list next to the skill. Each entry names the audit, the skill commit, the step that should have caught the error, and what the entry changed: a rule in SKILL.md, a planted case in the suite, or nothing.
3. Accept a change to SKILL.md when the five planted cases score as before and, for a change to steps 3 to 6, when blind reruns on IFBench lose no finding and add no false one. Two runs of one skill version report different findings, so this takes more than one run per version.

Done when: the list exists and holds the IFBench entries; SKILL.md or a reference file says how an audit's outcome and later defect reports reach it; and the acceptance rule has been applied to one change, such as a rule for one of the two gaps above.

comments.author: XiaoyuanWang111
comments.body:
A first pass through this loop, on the first gap: I tested three wordings of a rule for step 4 against controls. On the measures I used, the third passes the acceptance test in step 3; the limits are below.

Each run is a blind audit of the same IFBench grader through step 5, with one brief and one model (Claude Opus 5.5). The controls use SKILL.md of the follow-up to #10422. The records and the scoring are in the [score card](https://github.com/XiaoyuanWang111/audit-grader-suite/blob/1304d3a4729e294e588f83290c958a2acd5f39df/runs/SCORES-ifbench.md).

| | Control | Control | Examples | List | List | Spelled out | Spelled out |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Of the earlier audit's 81 fixtures that the grader gets wrong, the run's replacement grader gives the earlier label on | 56 | 58 | 66 | 69 | 77 | 70 | 75 |
| Of the 5 earlier findings that the first rerun lacked before its review: reported as findings, plus as decision entries | 3 | 2 | 2 | 0 + 1 | 3 + 1 | 3 + 2 | 3 + 1 |
| A numbered label tried on the word and sentence checks | no | no | no | no | no | yes | yes |

- Examples: "when an input form shows a wrong verdict in one check, such as a list label before a line, ..., apply it to passing responses of every other check". The run chose five edits of its own, and none was a list label.
- List: "try at least these edits: a list label before a line (`1.`, `-`), markup around a word, ...". Both runs applied every edit to every check that ignores it, and both wrote the label as `- ` before the first line. The grader's sentence splitter cuts after `1.` and not after `- `, so the list-label finding on `sentence:keyword` and `format:emoji` stayed out.
- Spelled out: "a numbered label (`1.`, `2.`) and a bullet (`-`) before each line". Both runs tried the numbered label. In one, it changes the grader's verdict on `sentence:keyword` in 12 of 12 edited responses and the bullet in none. Both report the behavior, one as a finding and one under a decision entry.

Every run with a list corrects more of the 81 fixtures than either control. Five runs of the last wording on the five planted cases lose nothing: 15 of 15 defects, 5 of 5 ambiguities as decision entries, 5 of 5 traps respected, no false finding.

Limits: each version has one or two runs. Both lists come from what earlier runs missed on this benchmark, so the IFBench runs show that a run does what the rule names, and only the planted cases speak for other graders. I scored the runs myself on the fixture battery and the five findings, without matching every finding to the earlier audit. One of the five, a comma after a repeated word, is still reported by one run in two.

The last wording, for step 4's bullet on property tests:

> Apply each ignored edit to a passing response of every check whose contract ignores it, not only to the check where it first came up. For a grader of text responses, try at least these edits: a numbered label (`1.`, `2.`) and a bullet (`-`) before each line, markup around a word (bold, italics, an HTML tag), typographic quotation marks around a word and a typographic apostrophe inside one, punctuation directly after a word, a blank line between lines, and a trailing newline. Put the word edits on a word that the check reads, such as the first or last word of a sentence. File each wrong verdict that an edit causes.

Would you like a PR with this rule and the error list of step 2, after the follow-up to #10422?

comments.author: chrismc91
comments.body:
What I think we need is a failure mode eval (or really any eval) for the skill that we can use to measure performance. That will let us do automated iteration and get to a better version over time. It also gives us confidence to integrate this skill as a general recommended check when we implement an eval.

I'd welcome a draft proposal for how to do skill evaluations generally, with the grader audit skill as a worked example to kick things off.

comments.author: XiaoyuanWang111
comments.body:
Proposal: evaluate a skill on a fixed set of cases. In each case, a fresh agent run with the skill installed works in a sandbox that holds only the case's inputs. When it finishes, scorers that the run never saw read its output folder and the case's answer key, and write metrics. Each skill version runs several times per case, and the rule that decides between two versions is fixed before the runs.

Kinds of case:

- Failure-mode cases: a narrow input that triggers a failure the skill has shown before, such as a defect that an audit missed, built on a grader that the change under test was not written from. A run could start from frozen outputs of the earlier steps and stop after the step that failed, so it would be short enough to repeat many times; no run has done this yet.
- End-to-end cases: a use of the skill through step 5 on a real target (through step 6 when reviewers can run), scored against the answer key of an earlier audit. Held-out cases are end-to-end cases that no change to the skill is written from; a held-out case whose runs were read to write a change becomes a development case.
- Small synthetic graders that every version must pass.

Answer keys are versioned. When runs find a valid defect that the key lacks, the key grows and the stored replacement graders are rescored.

The scorers read outputs whose format the skill specifies, so that they run unchanged for every run. For audit-grader, the output a program can call is the replacement grader, which the skill requires when an audit finds a defect in the grader's code. Calling it on fixtures whose labels an earlier audit settled (a fixture battery) measures how many of those fixtures the run's contracts get right, with no reading of its report. It does not show that the run found the defect: on IFBench, the first blind rerun's replacement corrects the fixtures of three earlier findings that its report lacks, because its contracts were right and no fixture tried the input. A second metric below covers that.

What the audit-grader runs so far say about the design. These are the blind runs in [`audit-grader-suite`](https://github.com/XiaoyuanWang111/audit-grader-suite/tree/8c81c5bb9f4413f747f1497017b41307c2b0b30b), all through step 5 and all on Claude Opus 5.5 in Claude Code.

- The small graders saturate. Eleven runs on five small graders with planted defects, across three skill versions, found every planted defect, made no false finding, and filed the planted ambiguity as a decision entry in 10 of 11 runs. They can catch a regression but cannot rank two versions.
- Runs of one version vary. A defect fixture is one whose label holds under every reading and that the grader gets wrong; on IFBench that is 66 of the 81 fixtures the grader gets wrong. A run's score is the share of a case's defect fixtures that its replacement corrects. Five pairs of runs with the same version on the same case differ by 1 to 4 fixtures on IFBench and 2 to 4 on the RLVR1 rewards below (seven comparisons: each RLVR1 run's one replacement is scored on both rewards). The pooled standard deviation is about 4 percentage points, a rough estimate that the baseline's runs should replace. At that spread, a two-sample t-test at the 5% level with 80% power needs about 4 runs per version to show a change of 10 points, and about 12 for 5 points.
- A change must be judged on cases it was not written from. The step 4 rule in this issue was worded from what earlier runs missed on IFBench. There, four runs with a list of edits in step 4 (two wordings) corrected 59 to 64 of the 66 defect fixtures, against 49 and 50 for two runs without it, a gain of about 17 points. On the two rewards of the instruction-following rows of Marin's Nemotron RLVR1 data, which an earlier unpublished audit had checked, two runs with the rule's last wording averaged 4 points more than two runs without it on the SkyRL reward and 2 points more on the gate ([score card](https://github.com/XiaoyuanWang111/audit-grader-suite/blob/8c81c5bb9f4413f747f1497017b41307c2b0b30b/runs/SCORES-rlvr1.md)), within the spread of two runs.
- Report labels vary. Two runs of one wording filed the same markup or list-label behavior differently, one as a finding and one as a decision entry, so a metric that counts findings moves with that choice.
- Output formats drift. The four RLVR1 runs gave their replacement grader four different entry points: `replacement.check_constraint`, `contract_grader.check`, `contracts_grader.check` and `replacement.check`. The scorer needed a map from run to entry point.
- Isolation has to be enforced. Each run was told to stay in its folder, and two of the four RLVR1 runs still read output files of their own background commands outside it. The reads were harmless, but an answer key in a reachable folder would not be safe.
- Runs are long. Eleven runs through step 5 on IFBench and the RLVR1 rewards took 43 to 80 minutes each, with 142 to 223 tool calls and 0.23M to 0.34M output tokens. Step 6's two reviewers, run in parallel, took 19 and 25 minutes on a sample of 458 verdicts. One decision between two versions on two end-to-end cases at 4 runs each is 16 runs, about 16 agent-hours.

Where it runs. The vendored Harbor has most of the parts:

- A task is an instruction, an environment and a `tests/` folder. The tests reach the sandbox only after the agent finishes. With `[verifier] environment_mode = "separate"`, they run in a fresh container that receives only the declared output files (`vendor/harbor/src/harbor/trial/trial.py`, `vendor/harbor/src/harbor_config/models/task/config.py`).
- The verifier can write several named metrics to `reward.json`, and `n_attempts` repeats each task.
- `--skill` installs skill folders into the agent's environment, and the job lock records each skill's sha256 digest (`vendor/harbor/src/harbor/skills.py`, `vendor/harbor/src/harbor/models/job/lock.py`). The version under test is that digest together with the task's instruction.

A case then becomes a Harbor task: the case folder in `environment/`, the brief in `instruction.md`, the answer key and the scorers in `tests/`. Missing:

- Claude Code, which every audit-grader run so far used. #11080 removed it from the vendored Harbor. Of the agents left, Codex, OpenCode and Pi copy installed skills into their skills folder, and Terminus-2 lists them in its prompt.
- A launch path for a provider's model, such as Claude through Anthropic's API. Marin's evaluation launcher points the agent at a Marin-served model through the model relay and rejects skills on the local backend (`lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/harbor/trial_driver.py`). Provider keys stay on the host, and the relay's Responses route has no tools, so Codex through the relay is untested. `experiments/rl_data_reviews/review_runtime/harbor_worker.py` runs a Harbor trial against the endpoint in its config, with the API key read from a host environment variable; a skill-eval runner could start from it.
- A separate verifier on Marin's path. The same driver raises an error for a separate verifier environment, and the local backend does not build images (`docs/harbor-integration.md`). A runner that calls Harbor's `Trial` directly, as `harbor_worker.py` does, skips that driver; whether a separate verifier then works with the model relay is untested.

TaskCompendium's `TaskSpec` also hides verifier files, but its resources are single inline files, which fit a case that is a folder of code and data poorly. To compare two versions, the `ab-test-zephyr` skill has a pattern to reuse: calibrate the threshold from repeated runs of one version, and report pass, regression, tradeoff or inconclusive.

Other skills. The same parts apply where a skill leaves an output that a program can check: for `review-pr`, cases from merged PRs whose bug a later commit fixed, with a scorer that checks whether the review names the lines that the fix changed; for `add-dataset`, a frozen data sample and hidden tests on the code that the agent writes. Skills that act on a cluster need a simulated environment, which this proposal leaves out.

Worked example: an audit-grader eval.

| Case | Kind | Answer key | Public |
|---|---|---|---|
| Five small graders: a math answer checker, a code execution grader, an LLM-judge pipeline, a JSON reward, an agent task verifier | small synthetic | 3 planted defects, 1 ambiguity and 1 trap (a behavior that looks wrong but follows the task text) each, with an oracle that implements the task text | yes, in `audit-grader-suite` |
| Marin's vendored IFBench checkers | end-to-end, development | the earlier audit's 143 public fixtures (66 defect fixtures) and 43 checker findings | yes, `xiaoyuanwang/ifbench-audit` on Hugging Face |
| The two RLVR1 instruction-following rewards: NVIDIA's checkers in the SkyRL reward, verifyit's checks in the task-curation gate | end-to-end, held out | 625 fixtures; 39 defect fixtures for the SkyRL reward, 65 for the gate | no |
| One per gap in this issue: an input form carried across checks; review verdicts that no decision entry explains | failure-mode | fixtures for the form or for the unexplained verdicts, on a grader other than IFBench | to build |

Today there is one held-out case, it is the same kind of grader as IFBench, and its pilot runs have been read. Plan step 2 adds a held-out case of another kind, such as an LLM judge.

Metrics:

- Fixture battery: of the answer key's defect fixtures, how many the replacement grader corrects, and of the fixtures the grader gets right, how many it keeps right.
- Defects shown: for each finding in the answer key, whether one of the run's own fixtures on that check gets a wrong verdict from the grader. On the small graders, whether a fixture's verdict changes when the oracle switches one planted defect off. A finding and a decision entry count the same, so this metric does not move with the filing choice. It is the metric of the failure-mode cases.
- Counterexample check: each finding's fixtures, run on the grader through `run_fixture.py` (below), must show the verdict that the finding reports. On the small graders, they also run on the oracle, and a label that the oracle contradicts is a false finding.
- Smoke results on the small graders: planted defects found, ambiguities filed as decisions, traps respected, false findings. They are scored by hand today; the output format below lets a program score most of them.
- Interval coverage on the small graders: whether step 6's interval for the grader's error rate holds the true rate, which the oracle gives. It needs step 6's reviewers and gives one yes or no per run, so it is reported and not used for decisions.
- Cost: minutes, tool calls and tokens per run, which the harness that #9020 asks for could also record.
- Run check: the model behind each call, read from the trajectory, since a harness can route subtasks to a smaller model. A run with an unexpected model is discarded.

Decision rule: with at least 4 runs per version, a version passes on a metric when its mean beats the baseline's by more than two standard errors of the difference, regresses when it falls short by more than that, and is otherwise inconclusive. Right fixtures kept and the smoke results vary between runs of one version too (on IFBench, 57 and 57 of 62 for two runs without the step 4 rule, 53 to 59 for four runs with it), so they get the same test. A change that targets one failure mode is accepted when its failure-mode case passes and nothing regresses; a change meant to improve audits in general needs a pass on the held-out cases; a change to cost or format, such as plan step 1, needs only no regression. At the pilot's held-out differences of 4 and 2 points, the step 4 rule would most likely be inconclusive on the held-out case even at 5 runs per version (power about 0.25 and 0.12), so it is judged on its failure-mode case.

Baseline: the skill after plan step 1 (#10422, its follow-up #11218, and the output format below), at least 4 runs per end-to-end case. Another agent or model needs its own repeats. The suite's 16 blind runs of the step 4 rule's wordings and controls (7 on IFBench, 5 on the small graders, 4 on the RLVR1 rewards) are a pilot.

Output format, tested on a local branch. SKILL.md asks for `fixtures.jsonl` (each fixture's entry point, arguments and label), `findings.jsonl` (each finding or decision entry with its fixtures), a replacement grader with the grader's entry points, and `run_fixture.py`, which runs one fixture on the grader, the reference implementation or the replacement. The script became part of the format after a run on the LLM-judge pipeline made up its own calling convention for entries that take a template, a question record or a judge client. Three fresh runs on three of the small graders wrote the files and found all three planted defects each. Through `run_fixture.py`, a scorer that knows nothing about the agent task verifier ran all 54 of its fixtures on the grader and the replacement.

Plan:

1. Land the output format above in SKILL.md, with relative paths in the replacement grader. One small PR.
2. Build one failure-mode case, for the first gap in this issue, on a grader other than IFBench, and measure its run time. Then build the other cases as Harbor tasks, add a held-out case of another kind, add an agent and a runner for a provider's model, and run the baseline.
3. Judge the step 4 rule of this issue on its failure-mode case.
4. Once two skills have an eval, add a short guide to writing one to `docs/dev-guide/agent-workflows.md`.

Open questions:

- Where answer keys live. A public answer key can enter training data, and an agent with web access can read it. The IFBench answer key is public; the RLVR1 answer key is not.
- Which agents and models. Every run so far used one agent and one model. Marin supports several agent vendors (#8982), and a skill could pass with one agent and fail with another.
- When it runs: on each PR that changes a skill, or on a schedule, and with what budget per decision.
- What result makes audit-grader a recommended check: for example, a minimum share of held-out defect fixtures corrected and of answer-key findings shown, and no false finding on the small graders.

If this direction works for you, I'll start with step 1 of the plan.

issues.author: chrismc91
issues.body:
GSM8K flexible extraction returns `[invalid]` for every response whose scored text starts with `Question:`. `extract_gsm8k_flexible_answer` ([vendor/evalchemy/eval/lm_eval_tasks/gsm8k/utils.py:32](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/07f2c7179f/vendor/evalchemy/eval/lm_eval_tasks/gsm8k/utils.py#L32)) first truncates the response at the earliest `GSM8K_STOP_SEQUENCES` match, and that list contains the bare string `Question:`. Chat responses are scored with the default `combine` content policy, which puts `reasoning_content` before the final answer. A model whose reasoning opens by restating the prompt ("Question: ...") is truncated to an empty string, so both filters score 0.

Muse Glimmer 30B does this on every item. A 20-item `gsm8k-0shot` run from `main` (`07f2c7179f`, group `20261111-141222-meta-models-Muse-Glimmer-30B-6d632b18278a488c9a9c1f2f396635b4`) scored 0/20 with every extraction `[invalid]`, while the same model scored 19/20 on `math500`. Rescoring the stored outputs with the leading restatement skipped gives 17/20.

Evalchemy already keeps textual stops out of chat requests for this reason (`chat_request_stops` in `vendor/evalchemy/eval/generation_stops.py`: servers apply stop strings to reasoning content and truncate models that restate the question). The scorer reapplies the same stop to the combined text afterwards.

Reproduce:
1. From `vendor/evalchemy`, run:
   ```python
   from eval.lm_eval_tasks.gsm8k.utils import extract_gsm8k_flexible_answer
   extract_gsm8k_flexible_answer("Question: Janet sells the eggs left after using 7 of 16, at $2 each.\n16 - 7 = 9 eggs, 9 * 2 = 18.\nThe answer is 18.")
   ```
2. It returns `'[invalid]'`. Without the leading `Question:` line it returns `'18'`.

Expected: a restated question in the reasoning does not discard the rest of the response, and the extractor finds the final answer.

The canonical port applies the same truncation before `final_text` ([lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/importers/evalchemy/scorers/harness_generation.py:195](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/07f2c7179f/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/importers/evalchemy/scorers/harness_generation.py#L195)). We have not checked whether its response text includes reasoning. Recorded #10197 GSM8K scores may be affected for any model that restates the question; the stored samples can be rescored without rerunning inference.

---

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 # Research

The [Evalchemy filter](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/vendor/evalchemy/eval/lm_eval_tasks/gsm8k/utils.py#L32) and [canonical scorer](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/importers/evalchemy/scorers/harness_generation.py#L194) both truncate at bare `Question:` before extracting an answer. When combined reasoning starts by restating the question, that stop matches at offset zero and flexible extraction sees an empty response. [PR #10927](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10927) changes canonical equivalence checks, but does not touch this truncation.

**Relevant code**
- [generation_stops.py](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/vendor/evalchemy/eval/generation_stops.py) — request and scorer stop policy
- [gsm8k/utils.py](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/vendor/evalchemy/eval/lm_eval_tasks/gsm8k/utils.py#L32) — vendored flexible extraction
- [harness_generation.py](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/importers/evalchemy/scorers/harness_generation.py#L194) — canonical flexible extraction

# Proposed Fix

The scorer receives a response starting `Question: ...`, truncates it to empty, and returns `[invalid]`. Trim leading whitespace and use the line-boundary `\nQuestion:` stop while scoring in both paths; keep the request stop policy, which is applied during generation. Add regressions for a leading restatement followed by a final answer and for a later, unrelated question.

spillover_issues.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
spillover_issues.body:
The scheduled hero GB200 canary did not reach its metrics report. Kueue preempted its 16-task training gang twice; the Actions wait step then timed out after 340 minutes while the retried gang was gated. Classification: **infra/scheduling**.

Reproduce:
1. Submit the [hero GB200 canary workflow](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/11307246720536581307a02347a52c23f21ba5d1/.github/workflows/marin-canary-hero-gb200.yaml) at batch priority and let one training task reach RUNNING.
2. Preempt the gang and leave its retry gated for admission. The [monitor](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/11307246720536581307a02347a52c23f21ba5d1/scripts/ci/iris_monitor.py#L228-L265) keeps `child_running=True` after the first start, so its queue deadline cannot stop the later wait. The 340-minute Actions step limit fires first.

Expected: A preempted canary that cannot regain capacity ends with a controlled capacity outcome before the Actions timeout.

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

- The [Actions wait step](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/43077898418/job/130722469486) dropped its queue timeout when a child task first ran at 21:40:03 UTC and timed out at 00:07:59 UTC. Metric reporting was skipped.
- Regional Finelog `cw-us-east-08a` / `iris.task_event` records `WorkloadEvictedDueToPreempted` for all 16 training tasks at 21:41:14 and 00:04:23 UTC. The coordinator task was deleted by a `NoExecute` taint at 22:52:16 UTC and retried.
- At 00:14 UTC, Iris showed the training job with two preemptions and 16/16 tasks BUILDING; all 16 pods were Pending with Kueue admission and topology gates. The [uploaded diagnostics](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/43077898418/artifacts/13902357791) captured the retried training tasks receiving SIGTERM during checkpoint restore after the second eviction.
- A local monitor simulation with one RUNNING task followed by 16 BUILDING tasks, a 1-second queue deadline, and a second poll at 10 seconds made two polls and did not cancel the parent.
- [Echo incident record](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/967) preserves the diagnostic sequence.
- This differs from [#10897](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10897), which fixed dropping the queue deadline before *any* task ran.

</details>

## Canary run context

- Lane: `hero-gb200`; date: 2026-11-11 to 2026-11-12 UTC
- Iris job: `/runner/hero-canary-43077898418-1-coord`
- [GitHub Actions run](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/43077898418)
- [Configured W&B run](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/hero-canary-43077898418-1)

spillover_issues.author: penfever
spillover_issues.body:
Establish a versioned cold-start SFT recipe that runs immediately after pretraining cool-down. The recipe should produce a model with the core capabilities needed by Marin's post-training and evaluation workflows.

The initial competency set is:

- Chat-template adherence and basic instruction following.
- Think blocks.
- Thinking across science, mathematics, legal, and medical contexts.
- Adaptive thinking effort.
- Model-name responses.
- Basic agentic tool use.
- Answer-format hardening.
- Task summarization.
- Resuming a task from a summary.

Related preceding work: #7321 and #7743.

Research issues:

- #8093: adaptive thinking effort.
- #8094: model-name response behavior.
- #8092: answer-format hardening.
- #8095: task summarization.
- #8091: resume tasks from summaries.
- #8090: cross-domain thinking and basic agentic tool use.

Done when:

- A recipe version identifies its parent checkpoint, tokenizer and chat template, data mixture and immutable revisions, training configuration, and export contract.
- The recipe has acceptance evaluations for every listed competency, with recorded baseline comparisons and failure criteria.
- The recipe can be run after a pretraining cool-down without experiment-specific manual wiring.
- The selected recipe and its evidence are documented in the repository.

comments.author: ravwojdyla
comments.body:
🤖 **Hero SFT tracking.** This issue now tracks cold-start SFT of the 535B-A23B Hero (Mochi) from its 262K checkpoint. Decision: use the 10.05 data. The SFT stage under Snowball v0.1 was 09.21, but 10.05 is the latest trained mix.

**Inputs**

- Start checkpoint: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/grug/hero-lce-log65536sq-step390k/2026.08.19.2/checkpoints/step-393491` ([#8435](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8435#issuecomment-6748198431)). `metadata.json` reads step 393491, not temporary. Size: 3.9 TB.
- Data: the 216-source "full A/B" mix of [Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.10.05](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.10.05): 79.65% SFT and 20.35% replay, packed at 262,144 tokens.
  - Code: branch `held/grug-sft-full-ab-4750-grouped` at `ce7c77a`.
  - Manifest: `gs://marin-us-central2/grug_sft/stores/full-ab-packed-2026.09.29.json`.
  - The stores and tokenizer `2026.09.18` have CoreWeave copies in `s3://marin-us-east-02a`, the Hero's region.
- Tokenizer: the SFT tokenizer maps IDs 128005 and 128011 to `<tool_call>` and `</tool_call>`. The Hero pin `marin-tokenizer@a5ca45f` keeps them reserved. The run needs the 10.05 seven-row LM-head anchor initialization and must ship the 09.18 tokenizer.

**Blockers**

1. The checkpoint's model (log scaling, floor 65536, power 2) exists only on the branch of draft #11044, which carries #10986. Main's `HERO_MODEL` would load this checkpoint with the wrong attention scale on the global layers.
2. There is no full-model Hero SFT launcher. The Hero trainer already reads loss-weighted packed batches with segment IDs. The launcher must port four parts from the 10.05 trainer: the store mixture, the anchor rows, the √32 special-token LR and the frozen router bias.
3. Export and serving refuse log scaling ([#11056](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11056) B5). No PR adds it. Until one does, the SFT model cannot be served or evaluated through vLLM.
4. No SFT load test of a Hero 262K checkpoint has run (#11056 C3).

**Plan**

- Size: about 6,909 updates of 176 × 262,144 positions on 11 GB200 NVL72 racks (CP4 × EP16), which is one epoch of the SFT stores.
- Cost: about 57 h at the pretraining step time, and about 4.4e22 FLOPs.
- Checks before the full launch:
  - CPU tests of the port.
  - A 20-step one-rack load, save and restore test.
  - A step-0 offline eval at 262K, compared with the finalist's clean macro of 1.6434.
  - The #11056 memory gate: at most 180.75 of 184.30 GiB.

**Open decisions**

- Learning rate and gradient clip. 10.05 used 5e-5 with no warmup, decay over the last 10% and no clip.
- Replay source. Proposed: the Hero's 262K Harrier mix.
- Run ID and DRI.

comments.author: ravwojdyla
comments.body:
🤖 **Hero SFT one-rack smoke tests, 2026-11-09.** The SFT procedure runs end to end on one GB200 rack, using the log-scaling model of #11044. It restores the Hero, reseeds the special tokens, trains on the 10.05 mix, saves and resumes. One recipe choice is open: with the router bias frozen as in 10.05, the Hero drops 5.8–8.1% of expert assignments.

**Setup**

- Shared by all runs:
  - start checkpoint `hero-lce-log65536sq-step390k/2026.08.19.2/checkpoints/step-393491`;
  - 16 × 262,144 positions per update;
  - CP4 × EP16 on `cw-us-east-08a`;
  - MuonH 3.2905e-5 and Adam 7.5934e-6, the Hero's final 262K rates, with clip 1.0;
  - the 10.05 one-epoch block schedule with the Hero's 262K Harrier mix as replay.
- Code: local branch `rav/hero-sft-launcher` on the #11044 head `80cadd6858`, at `8dd7cef524`. It is not pushed yet.
  - It adds `experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/launch_hero_sft.py`.
  - It adds SFT options to the Hero trainer: router-bias mode, the special-token reseed with a √32 learning-rate scale, and `data_start_step`.
- Checkpoints are under `s3://marin-us-east-08a/tmp/ttl=3d/rav/` and expire after 3 days.

**Runs**

| Run | Router bias | W&B | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| v1 | frozen | [hero-sft-smoke-v1](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe_sft/runs/hero-sft-smoke-v1) | Failed before the first update. Restore and reseed worked. Building the eval sets then asked each SFT store for a `validation` split, and the stores hold only `train`. Fixed by reading each store as a flat cache of its `train/` directory. |
| A, 20 updates | frozen | [hero-sft-smoke-v2](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe_sft/runs/hero-sft-smoke-v2) | Passed. Saved step-393511 (3.9 TB); details below. |
| B, resume A to 25 updates | frozen | same run as A | Passed. All 64 ranks loaded the run's own step-393511, did not reseed again, resumed the same W&B run, and saved step-393516. |
| C, 20 updates | update | [hero-sft-smoke-v3-update](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe_sft/runs/hero-sft-smoke-v3-update) | Passed. |

Smoke A details:

- Restore took about 2 min.
- All ranks reseeded the 7 special-token LM-head columns, with anchors {128006: 3560, 128007: 1984, 128002: 1781, 128003: 4320, 128005: 5507, 128011: 842, 128009: 128001}.
- Caches for the 415 components built in 1m13s.

**Measurements**

| | A: frozen | C: update | Finalist at the end of pretraining |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Drop fraction | 5.8% (step 393500) to 8.1% (393509) | 1e-4 to 3e-5 | about 2e-4 |
| Train loss at step 393500 (the same batch in both arms) | 0.646 | 0.698 | 0.81–0.95 |
| Gradient norm at step 393500 | 1.56 (clipped) | 1.65 (clipped) | about 0.17 |
| Dropless eval loss on Paloma after 20 updates | 1.712; macro 2.0399 | 1.742 | macro 2.0358 |
| Step time and peak memory | 23 s, 130.77 GiB | 23 s, 130.77 GiB | 29 s at 11 racks, 130.77 GiB |

**Findings**

- Snowball's SFT also froze the router bias. It ran with expert axis 1, and `capacity_overflow_rate_mean` is 0 in every Snowball SFT run. The Hero runs EP16 at capacity factor 1.5, so a frozen bias drops tokens.
- With the bias updating, the drops disappear. Train loss on the same batch and Paloma eval loss are higher over the first 20 updates. Twenty updates do not show which mode gives the better SFT model.
- The trainer's first-step eval never fires on a restored run. With `--eval-every 500`, the first SFT eval comes at step 393500.

**Open before the 11-rack launch**

- Router-bias mode. The launcher now requires `--router-bias`.
- Learning rate and clip, run identity and DRI.
- Merge #10986 and #11044, then land the launcher.
- Serving support for log scaling (#11056 B5), before the SFT model can be evaluated through vLLM.

At 11 racks the plan is 6,916 updates of 176 × 262,144 positions, about 57 h.

comments.body:
🤖 **Hero SFT plan, 2026-11-10.** The launcher and the expert placement are on `main` (#11136, #11149). The proposed run below does one epoch of the 10.05 mix on 11 racks. On one rack, this configuration drops 0.56% of expert assignments with a frozen router bias. Without the placement, the drop rate is 3.60%. Gate 1 needs sign-off and gates 3 and 4 need a reviewer.

**Proposed parameters (gate 1)**

| Parameter | Value | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Start checkpoint | `hero-lce-log65536sq-step390k/2026.08.19.2/checkpoints/step-393491` | Latest checkpoint from #8435; `metadata.json` step 393491 |
| Data | 10.05 full A/B mix: 216 CoreWeave stores, one epoch each | Latest validated mix; used as it is, without the Open-SWE fixes |
| Replay | Hero 262K Harrier mix, `--replay-fraction 0.2035` (20.43% at 11 racks) | 10.05 replay is Snowball pretraining data |
| Router bias | `frozen` (launcher default) | 10.05 recipe |
| Capacity factor | 1.625 | Highest that fits in memory; see below |
| Expert placement | `hero_sft_expert_placement_step393491.json` | Cuts drops from 3.60% to 0.56% |
| MuonH rate | 3.2905e-5 | Hero's final pretraining rate (1% of peak) |
| Adam rate | 3.2905e-5 | 10.05's pattern: one rate for both groups. Lower train loss, same eval |
| Gradient clip | 1.0 | Hero's clip; 10.05 used none |
| Topology | 11 racks, CP4 × EP16, 176 × 262,144 positions per update | |

The Adam rate applies to all `token_embed` rows, the router weights, `attn_gate` and the norm gains. The √32 update scale for the seven special tokens is separate.

**One-rack evidence.** All runs start from step-393491 on the same data order, frozen, MuonH 3.2905e-5, clip 1.0, 100 updates.

| Arm | Placement | cf | Adam | Train loss | Drops | Final dropless eval / Paloma macro |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| [1](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe_sft/runs/hero-sft-100-placed-cf1625) (proposed) | yes | 1.625 | 3.29e-5 | 0.5510 | 0.56% | 1.7089 / 2.0336 |
| [A](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe_sft/runs/hero-sft-100-placed-cf15) | yes | 1.5 | 3.29e-5 | 0.5524 | 0.89% | 1.7090 / 2.0338 |
| [B](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe_sft/runs/hero-sft-100-noplace-cf1625) | no | 1.625 | 3.29e-5 | 0.5581 | 3.60% | 1.7090 / 2.0336 |
| [4](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe_sft/runs/hero-sft-100-noplace-cf1625-adam7e6) | no | 1.625 | 7.59e-6 | 0.5613 | 3.67% | 1.7090 / 2.0343 |

- The order 1 < A < B < 4 holds in every 25-update quarter. The placement came from updates 1–25 of an earlier smoke, and A's drops stay flat through update 100.
- All arms run at 23.5–23.8 s/step with a peak of 130.8 GiB, the same as pretraining.
- Dropless eval loss does not separate the arms. Paloma macro improves from about 2.0386 at the first eval (step 393499) to about 2.034 in all four; the finalist ended at 2.0358.
- Arm A resumed from its own placed checkpoint, and no rank placed the experts or reseeded the special tokens a second time.
- Capacity factor: 1.75 and 2.0 fail the rematerialization check during compile. 1.6875, and 1.75–2.0 with a higher slop factor, compile but run out of memory in the first NCCL all-to-all. A higher factor needs a memory-layout change.

**Plan on `main` (`7521ea658f`).** Dry run: 6,916 updates (steps 393491–400407), 19 mixture blocks of 64,064 sequences, linear decay to 0.1× over the last 692 updates. That is 319.1B positions and about 4.4e22 FLOPs. At pretraining's 29.9 s/step on 11 racks, the run takes about 57 h. Checkpoints go under `expert-placement-1e80fa529585/` at 3.9 TB each, with one temporary resume checkpoint plus the final one.

```bash
IRIS_USER=marin uv run iris --config lib/iris/config/marin.yaml job run --no-wait --enable-extra-resources \
  --target-cluster cw-us-east-08a --priority system --system-reason "hero SFT" \
  --cpu 1 --memory 4g --max-retries 1000 --job-name hero-sft-fullab-step393k-coord \
  -e WANDB_API_KEY "$WANDB_API_KEY" -e IRIS_PORT_JAX 32614 \
  -- python -m experiments.grug.moe_hero_ep.launch_hero_sft \
    --run-id hero-sft-fullab-step393k \
    --initialize-from-checkpoint s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/grug/hero-lce-log65536sq-step390k/2026.08.19.2/checkpoints/step-393491 \
    --muon-lr 3.2905e-5 --adam-lr 3.2905e-5 --max-grad-norm 1.0 --replay-fraction 0.2035 \
    --dp-racks 11 --capacity-factor 1.625 \
    --expert-placement experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/hero_sft_expert_placement_step393491.json \
    --eval-every 500 --version 2026.11.10 --run
```

**Gates**

1. ⏸️ Select params: proposed above, needs sign-off.
2. ✅ SFT launcher on `main`: #11136 and #11149 merged, and the dry run above passes on `main`.
3. ⏸️ SFT data reviewed: needs a reviewer to accept the known caveats:
   - re-closed reasoning spans (#10400);
   - reward hacking in 17.3% of successful Open-SWE traces (#10865);
   - looping reasoning in 15.6% of sampled tokens ([report card](https://discord.com/channels/1354881461060243556/1355318637854199848/1569187938154057781)).
4. ⏸️ SFT smoke run reviewed: the arms above ran #11149 at `2f30fb76e9`. The merged #11149 also records the placement in each checkpoint's metadata and refuses a restore whose placement does not match. One short smoke and resume from `main` will confirm that path before kick-off.

Also before kick-off:

- 11 GB200 racks agreed with the Hero owners, and a `system`-priority submitter confirmed.
- Run ID (proposed `hero-sft-fullab-step393k`), DRI and babysitter named.
- vLLM evals of the SFT model need the log-scaling export (#11127).

**First-hour abort criteria** (from arm 1)

| Signal | Expected | Stop the run |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Restore | All ranks load step-393491 and log one placement and one reseed | A rank missing, or a second placement or reseed after a restart |
| Train loss | 0.4–0.7 | NaN, or at least 1.25 |
| Gradient norm | Below 1 on most steps; single spikes to about 8 | Above 10, or above 5 for several steps |
| Drop fraction | About 0.6%, under 2% per step | Above 3% sustained, or rising |
| Step time | About 29 s | Above 35 s sustained |
| First eval | Paloma macro within 0.01 of 2.0358 | Above 2.06 |

comments.body:
🤖 **Hero SFT attempt 1 stopped; relaunch after #11166.** `/marin/hero-sft-fullab-step393k-coord-471b9cf5` restored step-393491 on all 704 ranks, placed the experts and reseeded the special tokens once each, and trained step 393491 (loss 0.6029). It then failed in the drop-metric check: `ValueError: valid plus skipped assignments must equal the padded batch size` (`train.py:917`). The retry failed the same way, so the coordinator was cancelled. No checkpoint was written.

Cause: the MoE routing counts were float32, exact only up to 2**24. spillover_issues.author: karansag
spillover_issues.body:
🤖 
TL;DR: Levanter's Snowball forward differed from the served vLLM forward in four places: the MoE combine, the SiLU and sigmoid activations, the attention core, and an attention setting that an HF reload can drop. With (1)-(3) in place, the final zero-learning-rate precision run (one optimizer update at learning rate 0, with Levanter checked against vLLM) passed the precision gate with no failures and exported 502 tensors equal to the source. (4) has a fix in a draft PR; its effect was not measured.

Each diagnostic compares Levanter with a torch eager reference of the same model on the same inputs, and with stored vLLM log-probabilities and routes. BF16 means bfloat16. Each full-model run ran once, so there are no spread estimates. One repeated layer-0 dump ([second layer-0 diagnostic](https://gist.github.com/karansag/2ac0c5798b18bfdbec9a81b7090361d2#file-diag-l0-levanter-r2-reading-chukar-md)) found a run-to-run matmul-tiling noise floor of about 1 element in 40,704 at layer 0. "Route check" below counts layers (of 26) whose expert-route disagreement with torch stays within 2x torch's own batching noise and whose disagreements are near-ties.

| # | Difference | Found by | Measured effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | MoE combine (weighting and summing expert outputs) in BF16 | [combine diagnostic](https://gist.github.com/karansag/2ac0c5798b18bfdbec9a81b7090361d2#file-diag-moe-fix-r1-reading-chukar-md) | FP32 combine: contrastive max \|Δ log-prob\| vs vLLM 4.28 → 2.18 nats (limit 3.5 nats); top-1 disagreements 264 → 163 of 27,228 |
| 2 | XLA SiLU and sigmoid on BF16 inputs round differently from torch | [first](https://gist.github.com/karansag/2ac0c5798b18bfdbec9a81b7090361d2#file-diag-l0-levanter-r1-reading-chukar-md) and [second](https://gist.github.com/karansag/2ac0c5798b18bfdbec9a81b7090361d2#file-diag-l0-levanter-r2-reading-chukar-md) layer-0 diagnostics, [FP32-activation diagnostic](https://gist.github.com/karansag/2ac0c5798b18bfdbec9a81b7090361d2#file-diag-moe-fp32act-r1-reading-chukar-md) | 30-36% of single-op outputs differ; 0 with FP32 activations. Route check 10 → 22 of 26 layers |
| 3 | FA4 attention core uses a different operation order from torch | [attention diagnostic](https://gist.github.com/karansag/2ac0c5798b18bfdbec9a81b7090361d2#file-diag-l0-attn-r1-reading-chukar-md) | FA4 core differs at 247,091 of 814,080 elements (30.4%); torch order differs at 2 |
| 4 | HF reload drops `attention_implementation`, so attention can fall back to the FA4 core | [reload test](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10688) | not measured |

1. Combine. On the 8-GPU diagnostic, the FP32 combine also moved route set agreement with torch from 0.8939 to 0.8979. The route check stayed at 10 of 26 layers.

2. Activations. The 30-36% figure is the share of output elements that differ from torch when one SiLU or sigmoid op gets torch's exact BF16 input, at the embedding and layer-0 attention GatedNorms. SiLU differs at 35-36% and sigmoid at 30%. Each difference is one BF16 step. Computing both in FP32 and casting once gave 0 differing elements. The composite embedding output fell from 26.75% to 0.0002% differing, and the layer-0 attention norm from 46.80% to 0.024%. On the full model, overall Levanter-vs-vLLM route set agreement rose from 0.8984 / 0.8995 to 0.9123 / 0.9126 (two vLLM passes). Torch-vs-vLLM is 0.9120. That torch upcasts these ops internally is a hypothesis; the runs show only that the outputs match.

3. Attention. FA4 rounds unnormalized exponential tiles to BF16 and normalizes at the end. Torch normalizes the FP32 softmax and then casts to BF16. Levanter's `reference` path is further from torch (62.0% differing). A JAX transcription of torch's order (`torch_order`) matches torch at 2 elements. In the [full-model runs](https://gist.github.com/karansag/2ac0c5798b18bfdbec9a81b7090361d2#file-diag-flag-arms-r1-reading-chukar-md), layer-0 Levanter-vs-vLLM route agreement rose from 0.9503 to 0.9568 with `torch_order`. The 0.9503 run used a different code commit, so this comparison is not controlled. FA4 with XLA excess precision off reached 0.9572 in the same job as `torch_order`. The served vLLM uses FA3, which [handles the probability tile](https://gist.github.com/karansag/2ac0c5798b18bfdbec9a81b7090361d2#file-attention-backends-and-rounding-marten-md) closer to FA4 than to torch.

4. Reload. HF metadata does not carry Snowball's `attention_implementation`. After an HF reload the setting comes back as None, and on a GPU None selects `gpu_fa4_cute`. So a reloaded config that asked for `torch_order` would have run the FA4 core, with no error. No run is shown to have done so: the receipts of the last three zero-learning-rate runs record `torch_order` as loaded. The fix is in draft PR [#10688](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10688), which keeps the setting across the reload; its test checks that `torch_order` survives a reload. No run measured the effect of the fallback on a forward.

Result: the [final zero-learning-rate run](https://gist.github.com/karansag/2ac0c5798b18bfdbec9a81b7090361d2#file-lr0-r8-reading-chukar-md) ran on 32 H100s with `torch_order`, default XLA flags and an FP32 router bias, with the same recorded runtime recipe as two runs earlier. Gate failures: none. Its gate output equals the [previous run's](https://gist.github.com/karansag/2ac0c5798b18bfdbec9a81b7090361d2#file-lr0-r7-reading-chukar-md) except for output paths. Log-prob p99 / max against vLLM, in nats (limits 0.70 / 3.5): check 0.506 / 1.50, contrastive 0.553 / 1.98, long 0.581 / 2.76, past 2048 tokens 0.568 / 1.91. Contrastive candidate score p99 / max: 0.992 / 1.414 (limits 1.5 / 2.5). The layer-0 route line passed at ratio 1.0309 (limit 1.25): Levanter-vs-vLLM 0.956966 / 0.957031 against batched torch-vs-vLLM 0.958450 / 0.958257. The one zero-learning-rate update completed. The export audit found all 502 tensors byte-equal to the source. The all-layer route check (22 of 26 layers) and its variant against the served-vLLM floor (25 of 26) still fail; they were recorded as an accepted deviation and do not gate.

Fixes (all open draft PRs):
- (1) MoE combine: PR: [#10686](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10686)
- (2) SiLU and sigmoid: PR: [#10687](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10687)
- (3) attention order and (4) reload: PR: [#10688](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10688)
- Prerequisite: PR: [#10684](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10684) adds the route observer, the FP32 router dot and the function that keeps runtime-only settings after an HF reload.

Part of #10695.
